text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe pain and swelling in the left knee. I also have Pain intensifying over 2 months, Painful awakenings during night, No relief with ibuprofen. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand your urgency, and your symptoms of night pain and lack of response to NSAIDs are concerning for an inflammatory or neoplastic process. The blood work we requested will be critical, but could you tell me if you have noticed any visible warmth, redness, or a palpable mass over the knee joint?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Knees
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Left_Knee: A lesion in the distal femur with clear demarcation and non-invasive characteristics, suggestive of a benign process.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MRI findings of a well-demarcated, non-invasive lesion in the distal femur combined with your severe night pain and lack of response to ibuprofen strongly suggest a bone tumor. Given the specific location and characteristics, could you tell me your exact age and whether you have noticed any recent rapid growth of this area?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Tumor of Bone
